chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Sahl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that a man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام while he was with his companions, greeted him, then said:

To him: “By Allah, I love you and acknowledge your wilayah.” So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “You have lied.” He said: “Yes, by Allah, I do love you and acknowledge your wilayah,” and he repeated it three times.

So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “You have lied. You are not as you claim. Indeed, Allah created the spirits before the bodies by two thousand years, then He presented to us those who love us. So by Allah, I did not see your spirit among those who were presented. So where were you?” Then the man fell silent at that and did not reply to him.
And in another narration, Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “He was in the Fire.”

key_terms.أَتَوَلَّاكَ: I acknowledge your wilayah and devotion to your authority
key_terms.الْأَبْدَانِ: the physical bodies created after the spirits
key_terms.الْأَرْوَاحَ: the spirits created before bodily existence
key_terms.الْمُحِبَّ: the one who loves, meaning a true lover of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.رُوحَكَ: your spirit, referred to as known or unknown in the pre-temporal presentation

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain that the Imam recognizes the true followers of Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a man claiming love and wilayah for Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, but the Imam rejects his claim as false. The report presents the Imams’ recognition of their true followers through a pre-temporal reality of spirits and concludes, in another narration, that the man had been among the people of the Fire. The text highlights the theological significance of genuine wilayah and the Imam’s divinely granted knowledge.
